newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington new chief mandated to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington new chief mandated to cut costs.

text.p: Pilkington Plc said on Wednesday that it had appointed Paolo Scaroni as chief executive with the aim of accelerating the pace of cost cutting at the British glassmaking group.

Scaroni, who is currently president of Pilkington's automotive products world-wide division and joined the company in November 1996, replaces Roger Leverton, who acknowledged disappointment that efforts at the company had not yet meant value coming through to shareholders.
Chairman Nigel Rudd told Reuters, "We have done quite a lot of restructuring but we felt the pace of change was not fast enough in a very difficult industry."
"Roger (Leverton) has done a good job, but it is not good enough," he added.
Before joining Pilkington, Scaroni was executive vice chairman at Italian engineering group Techint.
Pilkington and Techint jointly acquired Italian glassmaker Siv from defunct state industrial holding company Efim in 1993. Pilkington has since bought out Techint's share in Siv.

Shares in the company were six pence higher at 121-1/2 pence by 1321 GMT following the announcement. Analysts said the stock has underperformed the all share index by around 40 percent for well over a year.
Scaroni's appointment follows a year that has included two profits warnings against a background of tough European markets and a strong pound.

Leverton said in a statement announcing the change that the group had made "significant progress" since 1992 in refocusing, but said trading conditions had been extremely difficult in certain key markets and said "results have been disappointing".
The company warned in March that annual profits would be below market forecasts but not less than 130 million pounds ($215 million). The average profit forecast at that time was 178 million pounds.
It has had particular problems in Germany, where demand for building products has fallen as the economy remains slack and unemployment has soared.

These conditions have forced the company to embark on a cost cutting drive aimed at Europe in particular, where sales volumes and prices of processed products have been affected by the slowdown in the construction industry.

Pilkington's restructuring efforts have seen its annual pretax profits for the year to March 31, 1996 slump to 55 million pounds from 144 million after a charge of 155 million pounds. Results for 1996/97 are due on June 5.

Rudd said that the company's main priority was to address problems at its European operations. He noted that building products in Europe has been a difficult area for the company and said that Germany's performance in particular has been very poor.
The company is currently in talks with German unions, where it employs 9,000 people, about the closure of processing and double glazing plants to cut capacity.
Rudd refused to disclose how many job cuts the company is seeking to cut in Germany.
"There is overcapacity in the European glass industry and it is difficult to see when there will be a big pick-up, but we are hoping for one later in the year," Rudd told Reuters.
